releases.name: Anka 1.0.1
releases.body:
**Anka 1.0.1** opens games stored as **.nup** packages.

Built from [`anka`](https://github.com/EddizEge/Anka/tree/anka) at `2d17a71ff0f0cf0c27b3d7207818fade9199b77b`; both programs carry this commit.

## Updating from 1.0.0

Close Anka, unzip **`Anka-1.0.1-win64.zip`** into your Anka folder and replace the files. Your `user` folder (settings, keys, firmware and saves) stays as it is.

New to Anka: follow the quick start in the [1.0.0 notes](https://github.com/EddizEge/Anka/releases/tag/anka-v1.0.0). Unzip into a new, empty folder, start `anka.exe`, and install your own keys and firmware.

## What's in 1.0.1

### .nup packages
- `.nup` ("Unencrypted (Archival) Package") is a container format from upstream Eglantine. It holds one title's base game, update and add-on content in a single file.
- Anka now **reads** .nup files. You can open them with **File › Load File…**, and they appear in the game list with their icon, name and version. `anka-cli.exe` and its launchers open them too, including from the `Games` folder.
- Mods (LayeredFS) and Anka's game-specific settings apply to games opened from a .nup, the same as for other formats. Anka finds the title ID before the game starts.

releases.name: Anka 1.0.0
releases.body:
First release of **Anka**, a Nintendo Switch 2 emulator for Windows, focused on performance.

Built from [`anka`](https://github.com/EddizEge/Anka/tree/anka) at `b7542ece8b5c695e2f01d5e46b74c0806d48ae96`; both programs carry this commit.

## Quick start

1. Unzip **`Anka-1.0.0-win64.zip`** into a **new, empty folder**. Do not unzip it into another emulator's folder: its Qt DLLs would replace that program's.
2. Start **`anka.exe`**. Anka keeps its settings, keys, firmware and saves in the `user` folder next to it (portable mode) and does not touch `%APPDATA%\eden` or other installs.
3. Install your own keys and firmware as with other Eden-based emulators. Anka includes no games, keys or firmware; only use what you legally own.
4. Settings: **Emulation › Configure… › Anka**. The first start picks *Recommended*, the setup we measured (with GPU Mode *Fast*, the default; it also turns Reactive Flushing off).

Coming from PokeDinner-Eglantine 2.0.0: back up its `nand` folder (your saves), then copy its `user` folder next to `anka.exe`.

Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) and a GPU with a current Vulkan driver. Qt and the Visual C++ runtime come with Anka.

## What's in 1.0.0

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.9.5
releases.body: # ARMSX2 2.9.5 What's new: ## Memory cards **Folder memory cards keep every save.** If your memory card's Type is Folder, every save is now written whole. A save made just before you left the app could come back blank or as the older version, because the card was written to storage between the save's data and its file entry; that can no longer happen. A new save that reuses a deleted save's space keeps its own name instead of reappearing under the deleted one's. A save file the device won't open for writing is still read, where the game showed it as damaged. New saves are created on storage that needs Android's own file access with the IOP thread on, and leaving the app rewrites nothing when nothing on the card changed. done by @bmdhacks

releases.name: ARMSX2 2.9.4
releases.body: # ARMSX2 2.9.4 ## New **Vulkan by default.** New installs start on the Vulkan renderer on every device whose driver reports Vulkan 1.1, and on Auto elsewhere. Existing installs keep the renderer they have. Auto now picks Vulkan on every Mali of the Bifrost G31, G51, G52 and G76 generation and of the Valhall generations (G57 to G78, G310 to G710, G615, G715, Immortalis-G715). done by @bmdhacks **MaliSX2 on every Mali it drives.** The GPU Driver list, the GPU card, first-run setup and the driver notice offer MaliSX2 on the Mali-G31, G51, G52 and G76, G57, G68, G77 and G78, G310, G510, G610 and G710, and G615, G715 and Immortalis-G715. The G31, G51 and G310 to G710 need MaliSX2 0.5.0 or newer. done by @bmdhacks

releases.body:
Automated nightly build for community testing (unsigned).

Every download is named `ARMSX2-nightly-DATE-COMMIT-PLATFORM`, so builds
from different nights stay distinguishable after you have downloaded them.

- macOS arm64: macOS-arm64.tar.xz
- Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-4K-pages.AppImage on most distros, or the 16K one on Asahi Linux and other Apple Silicon kernels (run getconf PAGESIZE if unsure)
- Windows arm64: Windows-arm64.zip
- RetroArch on Linux arm64: Linux-arm64-libretro-core.tar.zst, a 4K-page build
- Bare-display kmsdrm handhelds: Linux-arm64-SDL-handheld.tar.zst, a 4K-page build (Rocknix and Batocera run compositors, so use the Qt AppImage there instead)
- Android: Android-arm64.apk (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)
- iOS: iOS-arm64.ipa, unsigned, sideload it (installs as ARMSX2 Nightly, alongside the stable app)

Coming from an old nightly? Nightlies are now a separate app, ARMSX2 Nightly, next to stable.

- Android: stable cannot install over an old nightly. Back up your saves and memory cards, uninstall the old nightly, then install the stable APK.

releases.name: Cemu Plus 0.4.1
releases.body:
Android build of Cemu Plus, a fork of the Cemu Android port with Lossless Scaling frame generation.

## What's new

### Game updates
- **Use update** in the settings of a game, under Update, turns its installed update off, and the game runs as its base version. It's only shown for games with an update, and applies the next time the game starts. The game card shows the version the game runs as

releases.name: Copperline 1.1.0
releases.body:
Copperline 1.1.0 is the first feature release of the 1.x series. Hard drives can now run at the speed of the period drives each Amiga shipped with. The MMU-less 68EC030, 68EC040 and 68EC060 are new CPU choices. The JIT is much faster on fast-RAM code and heavy disk I/O, and has a new "fastest" speed. A500 CIA, interrupt and bus timing are corrected against measurements of a real A500. It also includes every fix made on the 1.x branch since 1.0.1.

## Before upgrading

- **Netplay peers must all run 1.1.0.** Players and spectators need the same build.
- **Recreate RetroArch save states after updating the core.** The core's states carry a build fingerprint that includes the release version.
- **Desktop save states from 1.0.x still load.** The CIA chunks are migrated to their new layout. A resumed 1.0.x state continues under the corrected timing, so it can drift from what 1.0.x would have produced (a factory A500 state from 1.0.1 still renders byte-identical frames). States saved by 1.1.0 do not load in 1.0.x, which reports that the state comes from a newer Copperline.

releases.name: Copperline 1.0.1
releases.body:
Copperline 1.0.1 is the first maintenance release for 1.0. Most of it fixes problems reported against 1.0.0: an AGA display fetch error, a blitter race on fast CPUs, warm reboots on the A3000 and A4000, the 68060 FPU at reset, the copperhf hard-disk driver, and a window-resize hang on Windows. Menu settings are now remembered between launches, and screenshots save the picture as you see it.

## Before upgrading

- **Netplay peers must all run 1.0.1.** Players and spectators need the same build.
- **Recreate RetroArch save states after updating the core.** The core's states carry a build fingerprint that includes the release version. Desktop `.clstate` files still load: the save-state format has not changed, and a 1.0.0 state resumes byte-for-byte as it does in 1.0.0.

releases.name: Copperline 1.0.0
releases.body:
Copperline 1.0.0 is the first stable release. It follows two weeks of testing of 1.0.0-rc.1 and is the 23rd release since the source went public on 14 June.

This release adds Smart framing and native 1:1 screenshots, more control over where and how the window opens, VHD hard-disk images, a fix for AGA sprites that use scan-doubling, and a Check for updates button that only contacts GitHub when you press it.

## Copperline 1.0 at a glance

- **Machines:** A1000, A500, A500+, A600, A1200, A3000, A4000, CDTV and CD32, with OCS, ECS and AGA chipsets and 68000 to 68060 CPUs, FPUs and MMUs.
- **Accuracy:** the CPU and custom chips run on one colour-clock timeline, with the chip bus shared out cycle by cycle. Timing is checked against a real A1200, A4000 and CD32, and 45 test programs are compared pixel for pixel on every change.
- **Ready to run:** the open AROS ROM is bundled, as are ROMs for the A2091, A4091 and IDE boards, the CD32 FMV module and the HRTMon freezer. WHDLoad packages and Amiga programs boot directly.

releases.name: Copperline 1.0.0-rc.1: the first release candidate for 1.0
releases.body:
This is the first release candidate for Copperline 1.0. If testing does not turn up problems that need a second candidate, the next release will be 1.0.0.

This cycle brings three- and four-player netplay on the desktop, debugger watchpoints on device registers with a timed trace of CD32 drive commands, a refreshed AROS ROM, and a review of the whole manual against the program, which also found and fixed a few mismatches in the program itself.

Please try your usual games, demos and configurations with it. Anything that worked in 0.21.0 and does not work here is exactly what a release candidate is for: [open an issue](https://github.com/CopperlineHQ/Copperline/issues) with the configuration and the software involved.

## Before upgrading

- **Netplay peers must all run 1.0.0-rc.1.** The wire protocol moved to version 3 to carry up to four players, so a 0.21.0 peer cannot join.
- **Recreate RetroArch save states after updating the core.** The core's states carry a build fingerprint that includes the release version. Desktop `.clstate` files from 0.20.0 and 0.21.0 still load; states from 0.19 and earlier do not.

releases.name: Copperline 0.21.0: spectators, four controllers and desktop fixes
releases.body:
Copperline 0.21.0 adds spectators to Netplay, connects four local controllers on desktop and in RetroArch, and reduces the work needed to put each frame on screen. It also fixes file-picker crashes and changes two defaults that could upset otherwise working games.

## Before upgrading

- **Clipboard sharing is now off by default.** It fits an extra autoconfig board, which changes the Amiga's memory layout. That caused a hang in Lotus Esprit Turbo Challenge under 0.20. Enable it explicitly with `--clipboard` or `[clipboard] share = true` when you want it. An existing configuration that explicitly enables sharing keeps doing so.
- **The CD32 FMV cartridge is now optional.** A stock CD32 starts with an empty cartridge slot. To use the bundled open FMV ROM, select **Fit** in the launcher's FMV row or set top-level `fmv = true`. A named `fmv_rom` still fits that ROM. Configurations that relied on the old implicit default need this setting for FMV playback; ordinary CD32 games no longer inherit the cartridge's changes to memory layout and boot timing.

Changes since the latest beta release:
- Fixed two UI issues (#843, #846)
- Fixed a bug in the CBM file system implementation (#853)
- Fixed a bug in the drive idle logic (#854)
- Fixed three drive-related VICE tests (#668, #674, #675)

Core and API

* Public API: The API now has as new shape. There are async counterparts (…Async) for state-changing calls, set is now setAsync, there is a new MemoryDebugger API, more getters, and suspend/resume coverage across the API.
* Threading: The command queue and message queue are now std::deque-based. Messages can carry exceptions. AudioPort is thread-safe. Cmd::CALL, TRACK_ON and TRACK_OFF are new.
* Messages: Msg::CONFIG is sent for every option change. ROM_LOADED, RSH_DONE and CONFIG_ERROR are new.
* RetroShell: It has the new architecture from vAmiga, with multiple shells and a single console per shell.
* Workspaces: A screenshot is now saved inside saveWorkspace().
* X-Ray: GPU X-Ray support is added, with a new XRAY_COMPOSITOR option.
* Shared libraries: utlib and rvlib were merged with the versions shared with vAmiga and Silicium.
* Cleanup: Header, include and namespace cleanups, plus removal of orphaned files.

Fixes

* Drive::isIdle() is fixed (#854).

This maintenance release primarily addresses issue #851, which prevented the app from running on the upcoming macOS 27 Golden Gate. It also includes internal code changes required to make the core compatible with the architecture of the upcoming Silicium emulator.
Removing beta status, as no significant bugs have been reported for some time.

## Refactoring

This beta release introduces substantial changes to the underlying code base. As part of the development of the RetroVault app, a new **RetroVault** library has been created. This library is now responsible for managing:

- File systems  
- Devices  
- All supported image formats  

RetroVault is designed as a standalone library and is also used in the latest version of vAmiga for the same purpose.

In addition, the new **utlib** library has been introduced. All utility functions previously embedded in vAmiga and VirtualC64 have been refactored into this more powerful shared library. This makes it easier for me to share common functionality among the different emulators. 

## Enhancements

- The disassembler now supports symbol files (#837)

## Bug Fixes

- Fixed a crash in the file system importer when importing excessively large folders (#841)  
- Fixed a bug in the VIC inspector that prevented selecting individual sprites in Tahoe (#840)

releases.name: msr2ds 2.1.0
releases.body:
Windows, Linux (x86_64 and ARM64), macOS (Apple Silicon) and Android (arm64).

## What changed since 2.0.9

A fix for the Android phones that crashed at the title screen in 2.0.9, and a pause screen redone for controllers and wide screens.

- **Android: no more crash at the title screen on Adreno 830 phones** (#58, #37). On Snapdragon 8 Elite devices (the Odin 3 and phones with the same chip), 2.0.9 crashed at the first 3D scene: the graphics driver's shader compiler crashed building 2.0.9's new per-material lighting. On Adreno GPUs, lighting now works as it did in 2.0.8, and the lighting code is back in the shape their compiler handled. Other GPUs keep 2.0.9's faster lighting. If 2.0.9 left the app in its safe graphics mode after a crash, this update clears it.
- **The pause screen fills the window**, now on by default (HUD tab: **Fit the pause screen to the window**). Its bars and background reach the window's edges, its buttons and text keep their shape, and the map fills the width, so you see more of the area.
- **The touch screen's menus are drawn from the game itself.** The title, the file select, the pause pages and the HUD's map are rebuilt from the game's own interface and pictures (or your texture pack's), sharp at any resolution, instead of a copy of the 3DS's small screen. Switching pause tabs now fades smoothly at the game's frame rate.
- **The pause map on a controller.** Left and Right go along the map's toolbar (D-pad icons beside it show this), and A chooses. On the map pins tool:
  - The D-pad or the stick chooses a pin. Up goes to the pins already on the map, and Down comes back to the bar.
  - A picks the pin up, the stick moves it, and A again places it. Pushed against the map's edge, it scrolls the map. B puts it back where it was.
  - X (Square on PlayStation) removes the map pin chosen; a box above the bottom-right corner shows the button.
  - Delete all is at the end of the bar.

releases.name: msr2ds 2.0.9
releases.body:
Windows, Linux (x86_64 and ARM64), macOS (Apple Silicon) and Android (arm64).

## What changed since 2.0.8

Mostly Android fixes, and faster lighting everywhere.

- **Android: "Not built yet" with the native code in place** (#58, #63). On some devices (an Odin 3 in #58), Android gives a `recomp-android` folder copied in from a PC an owner the app can't read. The app now makes the `recomp-android` folder itself, so a copy from the PC goes into a folder it owns. If a folder you copied in earlier can't be read, the launcher says so and what to do: delete that folder from the PC, then copy the two files from the PC's `recomp-android` folder (`libmsr_aot.so` and `module.json`) into the empty one the app makes in its place. A copy dropped inside the app's folder (`recomp-android/recomp-android`) is moved up. `launcher.log` says what the launcher found.
- **Android: GPUs without the 32-bit depth format with stencil** (#53). These (Adreno 6xx, such as the Adreno 640) now draw with the 24-bit depth format with stencil, the one Azahar uses on them, instead of 32-bit depth without stencil. On an Adreno 640 the game crashed at the first 3D in 2.0.7, at the first use of that depth buffer. This should fix it, but it isn't confirmed on that phone yet. The game's stencil effects work there now too.
- **Android: up to 1.1 GB less memory** (#66). On GPUs that can't scale a depth image down, the game set aside about 1.2 GB for reading depth back at up to 10x, whatever the resolution. That memory now follows the resolution you play at: about 140 MB at 2x, 270 MB at 4x. Every 2 seconds the log now also says how much memory the game uses and how much the device has left (on Android and Linux).

releases.name: msr2ds 2.0.8
releases.body:
Windows, Linux (x86_64 and ARM64), macOS (Apple Silicon) and Android (arm64).

## What changed since 2.0.7

- **New menus.** The settings menu (F1 or Select) and the launcher have a new look: a dark glass panel, a tab strip you switch with LB and RB, and on/off switches in place of checkboxes. Every option is where it was. The **Controls** tab is now one page that scrolls as a whole, with headings. Before, its bindings scrolled in a box two rows tall.
- **Quick save and Quick load on a controller.** Hold **Back** and press **LB** to quick save, or **Back + RB** to quick load. F5 and F8 still work. To use other buttons, choose the button beside Quick save or Quick load (Game tab or Controls tab), then hold the buttons you want until its 5-second count ends. A combo needs two buttons or more, and the triggers count. Because Back is in these combos, Back on its own now opens the menu when you let go of it, not when you press it.
- **Dump game textures works** (#64). Turn it on on the Textures tab and play. Each texture the game draws is saved once as a PNG named the way Azahar names it, in `dump/textures/00040000001BB200/` in the user folder, along with the `pack.json` a pack needs. The tab counts them and has a button to open the folder. Packs made from a dump also work in Azahar.
- **The minimap stays on Samus.** It found her marker by its red on the bottom screen, so a Missile Reload Station's red icon could pull it away. It now reads where the game itself draws her marker.
- **The Grapple Beam and Ice Beam slots** show only once Samus has those beams. Before that, the game's dim placeholder showed in the HUD as a circle.
- **Screens the game shows during play**, such as an elevator's or a Teleport Station's map, now show over the view the way the pause menu does, instead of beside it. After one of the game's messages, such as the Aeion abilities screen after picking one up, they now appear right away instead of a few seconds later.

releases.name: msr2ds 2.0.7
releases.body:
Windows, Linux (x86_64), macOS (Apple Silicon) and Android (arm64).

## What changed since 2.0.6

Several of these come from comparing the game's renderer with Azahar's (the emulator our 1.x releases were built on), which has years of fixes for phone graphics drivers.

- **Android: phones with Mali graphics** (#52, #54: Unisoc T820, Helio G99 and others), where the screen stayed black while the game played on. Mali's driver sometimes ends a wait for the GPU early with an error. The game ignored that and reused memory the GPU was still drawing with. It now waits again, as Azahar does. It also no longer stalls for good when the next frame's image can't be had, and on Mali it sets the depth and stencil state the way Azahar does there. This hasn't been confirmed on a Mali device yet: please try it and attach `msr-native.log` to #52, whether it works or not.
- **Android: Adreno 6xx phones closing a few seconds into the game** (#53). Until a vertex program's translation is ready, the phone's GPU ran it through a large general-purpose shader that older Adreno drivers can't handle. On Android those draws are now shaded on the processor instead, as Azahar does. Effects may take a moment longer to appear the first time.
- **Android: when the app closes while starting** (#58). If a start ends while opening the graphics, the next start opens them in a simpler, safer way, one step further each time, and stays that way until the next version. The log of the start that failed is kept as `launcher-crashed.log` or `msr-native-crashed.log` beside the new one: please attach both.
- **Android: less work for phone graphics** (#37). A frame's work is no longer sent to the GPU in the middle of a pass, which made a phone's GPU save and reload the whole picture an extra time: 11 passes a frame in gameplay instead of 13. Textures also skip a check most of them don't need. A read past the end of a buffer can no longer crash the GPU (`robustBufferAccess`, as Azahar turns on).

releases.name: msr2ds 2.0.6
releases.body:
Windows, Linux (x86_64), macOS (Apple Silicon) and Android (arm64).

## What changed since 2.0.5

- **Android: phones with Vulkan 1.1 can now run the game** (#53). Phones and handhelds from about 2019 to 2021 (Adreno 6xx and Mali-G7x graphics, such as the Galaxy S10 and Note 10) have Vulkan 1.1 but not 1.3. Until now the app couldn't use their graphics at all: a black screen and an error message. It now draws with Vulkan 1.1 there, by itself. This is new and hasn't been confirmed on a phone yet: if you have one of these, please try it and attach `launcher.log` and `msr-native.log` from the app's user folder to #53, whether it works or not.
- **Android: less wasted work on phone graphics** (#37). Most of each frame's passes are full-screen effects that never use the depth buffer, yet a phone's GPU loaded and saved it for each of them. Where the graphics driver supports it, they now leave it alone. `msr-native.log` also shows where the GPU's time goes, to help with the next improvements.
- **Android: when the window can't open** (#53, #54), the app now tries once more, logs more detail about why, and the message no longer gives a PC's advice. If you still get it, please attach `launcher.log` to an issue with your device's name.
- **New Display options** (#51, #25):
  - **Anti-aliasing (FXAA)** smooths the game's jagged edges, with either upscaling.
  - **Smooth texture packs** filters a texture pack's textures smoothly, also where the game shows its own with sharp pixels.
  - **Brightness, Contrast and Saturation** (50-150%), with a button to put them back as the game draws them.
- **Windows: "Python could not be unpacked"** (#47). When Windows' own unzip tool fails on the build tools' Python, the launcher now tries PowerShell's instead.

releases.name: msr2ds 2.0.5
releases.body:
Windows, Linux (x86_64), macOS (Apple Silicon) and Android (arm64).

## What changed since 2.0.4

- **OpenGL for graphics without Vulkan 1.3** (#34, #24). On computers whose graphics have no Vulkan driver (such as Intel's before its 6th-generation processors on Windows) or only an older Vulkan, the game used to draw on the processor, which is slow. It now draws with OpenGL 3.3 instead, at the internal resolution you choose. The Display tab has a new **Graphics API** setting under *For slower computers*: **Automatic** (the default) uses Vulkan where the graphics have Vulkan 1.3 and OpenGL otherwise, or choose Vulkan or OpenGL yourself; **Restart now** applies it. OpenGL has no HDR. The first time an effect appears, OpenGL prepares a shader made for it in the background (a slower general one draws it meanwhile); these are kept in `pwr_gl_programs.bin`, next to `pwr_shaders.bin`, so later starts load them quickly. On Linux it is included but hasn't been tried yet: if your graphics have no Vulkan 1.3, please report how it goes. The Mac is unchanged: it always uses Vulkan (MoltenVK, included) and has no Graphics API setting.
- **Vulkan: the saved shaders are rebuilt once.** After the update the game rebuilds its saved vertex shaders (`pwr_shaders.bin`) in the background the first time each one is needed. Nothing to do; the first minutes may run slightly slower on slow devices.

## Getting it

- **Already have 2.0 or later:** open msr-native. The Game tab offers 2.0.5: click **Update now**. On a Mac, if it only offers the download page, the app is running from the folder it was unzipped in: move `msr-native.app` to Applications, open it from there and update.
- **Windows (x64):** download `msr2ds-2.0.5-windows-x64.zip`, unzip it anywhere you can write to and start `msr-native.exe`. `msr-native-direct.exe` starts the game without the launcher, for a shortcut, Steam or a frontend.

releases.body:
## Added NetPlay Public Rooms

Until now, NetPlay worked over the internet with no account, no relay, and no service to trust. The one thing it could not do was find you an opponent: you still had to know someone already, and swap an IP address with them by hand.

**Public Rooms** is that missing half. It's an optional board where hosts advertise the game they are hosting, so anyone with the same ROM can tap it and connect.

What it is *not* is a relay. The board introduces two players and then steps out of the way — the match still runs directly between the two devices, exactly as it did before, and nothing about it passes through any server of mine. 

### On the board

* **Room codes.** Every room gets a short code you can pass to a friend. 
* **PIN rooms.** Tick *Require PIN* and the room still appears, marked as protected, but only the people you told can get in. The PIN itself never reaches the server — only a hash of it does.
* **A color-coded connection forecast.** Green, amber, or red per room, based on what STUN actually measured about both routers rather than a guess. Two symmetric NATs with no way through show red and refuse the join.

- **Fixed: the multi-second freezes.** A draw whose pipeline was still compiling used to block the renderer with an *unbounded* wait on the compile queue. releases.name: Moonlight Android v12.1
releases.body:
- Adjusted bitrate calculation logic to provide consistency across codecs, HDR settings, and local/remote streaming

[^1]: Requires upcoming Sunshine v0.22.0 release or the latest Sunshine nightly build

releases.name: Moonlight Android v12.0.2

releases.name: Moonlight Android v12.0.1
releases.body:

- Disabled gamepad motion sensors by default on Android 12 as a workaround for an Android 12 bug that randomly crashes Moonlight
- Fixed analog sticks not centering properly in some cases
- Adjusted bitrate handling of AV1 to be consistent with HEVC
- Fixed handling of some unusual H.264 and HEVC streams

releases.name: D2Android 1.6.0
releases.body:
- Skill buttons: every button casts its own skill, there is no left or right any more. Put skills on the buttons with **Assign Keys**: tap a button and pick its skill from the list, **Clear** empties it. The buttons are kept per character and taken over once from your game's hotkeys; your saved game is not changed. An aura's button switches the aura on, and it keeps running while you attack.
- Skills from items work on the buttons too, such as Teleport from Enigma or a staff, and charges.
- Teleport at once is now on by default: a tap jumps right away, holding keeps jumping, like Diablo II: Resurrected on a controller. Switched off (Settings › Controls › Skill buttons) you aim with the ring and jump when you let go, now without a pause.
- Joystick: it now stays where your thumb comes down. "Follows the thumb" is still there and no longer wanders off to the right; its dead zone can be set.
- Opacity: the joystick and the game buttons can be made see-through, from 20 to 100 %.
- Taps on the game's own buttons, such as its skill buttons at the bottom, land where you tap. The pointer no longer ends up in a corner of the screen.

releases.body:
What's new in 0.78

For players
- **32-bit devices:** one APK now holds both ARMv8 (arm64-v8a) and ARMv7
  (armeabi-v7a). Android picks the right one on install, so 64-bit devices
  always run the 64-bit version. OpenGL ES 3.0 is still required.
- **Screen orientation:** the setting now applies to the launcher as well as
  the game and takes effect at once. Auto respects the system rotation lock.
- **Sound:** the audio buffer margin now adapts to the device.
- **Launcher:** new Advanced screen with a Debug mode switch. With it off,
  nothing is written to the log.
- **Logs:** new screen under Data to export, share or send logs to the
  developer, or clear them.

Under the hood
- **Most of the game is now ported C++:** - game code is moving from recompiled to ported native ARM code.
- **Old processor code removed:** x87 emulation is gone from the generated
  code, and the whole game runs in 24-bit floating point. MMX, CPU detection
  and the Pentium FDIV workarounds are removed too.

Known limits
- ARMv7 has only been tested in the 32-bit mode of a 64-bit phone, not on a
  real 32-bit device, so speed on older hardware is unknown.

releases.name: v0.77
releases.body:
What's new:

### For players
- **Dynamic Fullscreen for races.** A new Screen Size option that fits the race to your phone's shape (20:9, 16:9, tablets) with no black bars, you can find it in Resolution tabs in-game Graphics settings. The view widens to the sides and the HUD keeps its proportions. It is the default for new imports. 
- **Options on the first screen.** The "NFS Web Site" button is now "Options...", so the settings are one tap away.
- **Gamepads: Analog or Digital** (Controls → Gamepads). In Digital mode you steer with the D-pad and use the triggers for gas and brake, like a keyboard.
- **Force feedback: one choice, Off / Phone / Gamepad**, instead of two separate switches. The in-game Stick Volume slider now actually sets the vibration strength (it used to always be full).
- **Dead zone and saturation** from the game's own Dead Zone screen now work, separately for the stick and each trigger.
- **The demo movie no longer freezes** on its last frame.
- **Split screen** uses the Modern Patch layout.

### Under the hood (same behaviour, now native code instead of recompiled)

releases.name: v0.76
releases.body:
What's new:

- New launcher UI on Compose.
- Network races work: phone with phone over Wi-Fi (IPX or TCP/IP), and phone with a PC running the Modern Patch over TCP/IP, as host or client.
- Disc image import: the launcher reads the game straight from an ISO or BIN/CUE image, on the first start and on the Data screen.
- Faster and cooler: the renderer driver and about fifty of the game's heaviest functions now run as native code. Each was checked bit for bit against the original. Removed voodoo2a emulation wrapper - now GPU code is fully native OpenGLES. 
- Rear-view mirror like the main view: full draw distance, track detail, full-size cars, sky with clouds and lightning, car lights and headlights.
- Fixed bugs on certain devices with saves.

releases.body:
## Security: Steam token redaction in logs

GameHub Lite 5.1.8 fixes a logging issue where Steam authentication-related values could appear in diagnostic logs. 
In some cases, logs could include fields such as `steamToken`, `refreshToken`, or `accessToken` from Steam login/launch flows.

**Publicly posted logs containing these fields should be deleted or redacted.**

### IMPORTANT

This should go without saying but If you find any security issues, please reach out **PRIVATELY**. 
I have not checked if this issue is still present in recent GameHub versions, already ruined my one day off I was spending with my family by the person who reported this publicly and I do not plan on spending any more time on this.

### Changelog

The fix adds centralized log redaction for Steam/auth token fields, Steam QR login URLs, JWT-like token strings, and launch command token arguments before logs are written. This covers the app loggers, JavaSteam logging, and the PC launch-log file writer.

This release also pins local patch builds to `apktool 2.12.1`

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Producdevity/gamehub-lite/compare/v5.1.7...v5.1.8

releases.name: GameHub Lite v5.1.6
releases.body:
# GameHub Lite v5.1.6

This release fixes an actual app-side launch issue, and yes, also exists because apparently backend fixes do not count unless there is a fresh APK attached to a GitHub release.

The main app fix is for devices where GameHub would silently refuse to launch games when the `getUnknownDevices` / `startType` API path returned a `404`. Instead of failing closed and doing absolutely nothing, the app now falls back like it already did for the no-internet path.

Confirmed affected and fixed:

- AYANEO Pocket FIT
- Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 / Adreno 750
- Android 14

### Backend changes

More work happened in [gamehub-lite-api](https://github.com/Producdevity/gamehub-lite-api), because that is where a lot of compatibility and component delivery work lives now.

Backend changes since the `v5.1.5` release include:

- Updated simulator response timestamps so stale responses get refreshed.
- Added release asset verification and MD5 checks for GitHub release assets.
- Updated component manifests, timestamps, deprecated component removal, and total counts.
- Cleaned up SteamAgent2 manifest naming.
- Removed drivers that were already added in the latest GameHub manifest.

Apparently that makes it look like nothing happened, so here is an app release too. I will make a useless release every time we improve something that gets served via the server. 

### Backend changes

The main work happened in:

- [gamehub-lite-api](https://github.com/Producdevity/gamehub-lite-api)
- [gamehub-lite-worker](https://github.com/Producdevity/gamehub-lite-worker)

Recent backend-side work includes updated component manifests, new/updated container components, imagefs updates, corrected component counts, proxy/URL updates, and fixes around component list handling.

In particular, the worker/API side is where most compatibility and content fixes now happen. If something starts working without an APK update, that is why.

releases.name: ExaltDS 0.1.2
releases.body:
**New (experimental)**
- **HD cutscenes from your own video.** If you have your own HD copy of Awakening's anime cutscenes, such as a rip of the *Fire Emblem: HD Movie Collection* Blu-ray or another recording, ExaltDS can play your HD version in place of the game's 400×240 movies. The 3D cutscenes stay as they are.
  - **Nothing is included.** This release contains no HD cutscenes, video files or pictures from the game. ExaltDS only uses the video you choose and your own game file.
  - **How the import works:** in the sidebar, open **Mods / textures**, choose **HD movies from your video…** and pick the video file.
    - ExaltDS decodes the game's own movies from your copy and searches your video for each of the 14.
    - It finds where each one starts, any black bars, how the picture is framed, the frame rate and the brightness, then matches it to the game frame by frame.
    - It then renders the matched frames into HD clips on your device, with the device's own video encoder, and checks each clip.
    - On the AYN Thor this took about 8 minutes for a 15-minute video, with all 14 movies found and 99% of frames in HD. Then use **Apply and restart**.
  - **During play,** ExaltDS recognises each frame of a movie as the game plays it and draws your HD frame of the same moment over it. The game's own sound and subtitles stay. Anything your video doesn't have, such as a missing movie or a fade added by whoever recorded it, plays as the original.
  - **What video works:** one file holding the movies, in any order. It can have intros or other footage between them, and some movies can be missing. MP4, MKV, TS or AVI with H.264, HEVC, MPEG-2 or VP9 video, progressive or interlaced.
  - **Experimental:** tested on the AYN Thor with a 1080p recording. Disc rips (interlaced or 23.976 fps) haven't been tested yet. The HD clips take about 0.6 GB; **Remove HD movies…** deletes them.

**Setup:** open ExaltDS, choose your decrypted `.3ds`/`.cci`/`.cia` (and the DLC `.cia` if you have it), tick Naga's Tear if you want it, and press Set up. The game's code is compiled on your device; about 5 minutes on an AYN Thor. No game files are included.

**In this release**
- On-device setup with a bundled compiler (LLVM/Clang 21), the feet mod and Naga's Tear built from your copy.
- Naga's Tear (experimental): Recall Fate in the battle map menu returns to before any action or turn of the last 5 turns, with each action named (Attack, Wait, Move, Dance, Staff, Item, Pair Up, Separate, ...).
- 16:9, up to 4x resolution, 60 fps combat, HD texture packs (bring your own).
- Sidebar (Back in game): Quick Save / Quick Load, save slots, performance monitor, clock switch, mods, GPU drivers, opt-in anonymous diagnostics, Check for updates.

**Known limits:** tested on one device (AYN Thor, 16 GB). US release only. Setup runs a compiler on every core; 8 GB of RAM or more is recommended. A first-time setup on a fresh install, DLC and `.cia` input are not yet tested.

teton-dev-exaltds.latest_body:
**New (experimental)**
- **HD cutscenes from your own video.** If you have your own HD copy of Awakening's anime cutscenes, such as a rip of the *Fire Emblem: HD Movie Collection* Blu-ray or another recording, ExaltDS can play your HD version in place of the game's 400×240 movies. The 3D cutscenes stay as they are.
  - **Nothing is included.** This release contains no HD cutscenes, video files or pictures from the game. ExaltDS only uses the video you choose and your own game file.
  - **How the import works:** in the sidebar, open **Mods / textures**, choose **HD movies from your video…** and pick the video file.
    - ExaltDS decodes the game's own movies from your copy and searches your video for each of the 14.
    - It finds where each one starts, any black bars, how the picture is framed, the frame rate and the brightness, then matches it to the game frame by frame.
    - It then renders the matched frames into HD clips on your device, with the device's own video encoder, and checks each clip.
    - On the AYN Thor this took about 8 minutes for a 15-minute video, with all 14 movies found and 99% of frames in HD. Then use **Apply and restart**.
  - **During play,** ExaltDS recognises each frame of a movie as the game plays it and draws your HD frame of the same moment over it. The game's own sound and subtitles stay. Anything your video doesn't have, such as a missing movie or a fade added by whoever recorded it, plays as the original.
  - **What video works:** one file holding the movies, in any order. It can have intros or other footage between them, and some movies can be missing. MP4, MKV, TS or AVI with H.264, HEVC, MPEG-2 or VP9 video, progressive or interlaced.
  - **Experimental:** tested on the AYN Thor with a 1080p recording. Disc rips (interlaced or 23.976 fps) haven't been tested yet. The HD clips take about 0.6 GB; **Remove HD movies…** deletes them.

releases.body:
# 🛡️ [MOD] Exiled Kingdoms LAN Multiplayer — 2.0!

Hey everyone! Another update to the **LAN Multiplayer** mod for Exiled Kingdoms.

Here's the full summary:

---

## ⚔️ NEW — LAN Multiplayer Bug Fixes

### 🐛 Bug: Crash when entering Cities
- **Problem:** When entering some cities, the game would crash and close.
- **Fix:** Problem fixed, and you can now teleport and enter cities perfectly.

### 🐛 Bug: Monsters ignored the CLIENT when the HOST was far away
- **Problem:** Monsters only attacked when the HOST was nearby. If only the CLIENT approached, the monster would remain still.
- **Fix:** Detection now compares the HOST and all CLIENTs present on the same map and returns the **closest** to the monster as the target.

### 🐛 Bug: Incorrect monster level scaling in co-op
- **Problem:** Monsters scaled based on 0+ (extra players). × 2), resulting in level 2 Goblins in a session with 2
- **Correction:** Now uses the Bestiary's `minlevel` as a base before applying the LAN difficulty multiplier. Example: Goblin (base level 4) + 2 players = level 6. Yeti (base level 18) + 2 players = level 22.

### 🐛 Bug: CLIENT couldn't reduce HOST's HP in the PVP Arena

releases.name: v0.10.69 — Older processors without AVX
releases.body:
## Changes

- **Older processors without AVX (#432).** Windows and Linux PCs whose processor has no AVX can now start the game. Examples are 1st-generation Intel Core i5/i7 and the Pentium or Celeron of that time.
  - **What was wrong:** the game closed straight away with an "illegal instruction" error (`0xC000001D`) on these processors. It had only been built for processors with AVX.
  - **What changed:** the download now holds a second copy of the game built without AVX. The launcher checks your processor and picks the right copy by itself, so there is nothing to set.
  - **What to expect:**
    - The game runs slower on such old processors.
    - It still needs a processor with SSE4.2, so Core 2 and Phenom II processors can't run it.
    - On Windows, PCs from that time often have graphics cards without Direct3D 12 or Vulkan. Choose **Launcher › Graphics › Direct3D 11 (experimental)** on those.
  - The Windows and Linux downloads are about 17 MB and 19 MB bigger. Android, macOS and iOS are unchanged.

For #432

Everything else is the same as [v0.10.68](https://github.com/YuutaTsubasa/Free-Riders-Recompiled/releases/tag/v0.10.68).

## Validation

releases.name: v0.10.68 — Dolphin Resort water ski above 60 Hz
releases.body:
## Changes

- **Dolphin Resort water ski above 60 Hz (#410).** With **Test options › Gameplay › Race step rate** above 60 (for example 120 or 144):
  - **What was wrong:** on the Dolphin Resort water-ski tow, the racer turned round and rode backwards behind the boat. The camera then looked at the racer's face and swung low beside them.
  - **What changed:** the tow now behaves the same at every frame rate, so the racer rides behind the boat facing forward and the camera stays behind them. At the default 60 Hz nothing changes.

For #410

Everything else is the same as [v0.10.67](https://github.com/YuutaTsubasa/Free-Riders-Recompiled/releases/tag/v0.10.67).

## Validation

- **Windows x64 package, #410: Dolphin Resort Expert water ski with Super Sonic (unmanned, both Super Sonic options on), at Race step rate 144 and 60:**
  - Super Sonic rides behind the boat facing forward at both rates; the camera stays behind him.

releases.name: v0.10.67 — Hold to skip story scenes and movies
releases.body:
## Changes

- **Skipping story scenes and movies now needs a hold (#426).** A tap or an accidental touch no longer skips anything:
  - **Story scenes** (for example in World Grand Prix) skip only while you **hold** START, or keep your finger on the screen on Android, until the circle fills. Let go early and the circle drains and the scene goes on.
  - **Movies** skip when you hold START, A, B or Back for half a second. A quick tap, or Android's back swipe, no longer ends them.
  - The startup logos (ESRB, SEGA, Sonic Team) still skip with a press.

For #426

Everything else is the same as [v0.10.66](https://github.com/YuutaTsubasa/Free-Riders-Recompiled/releases/tag/v0.10.66).

## Validation

- **Windows x64 package, #426: Eggman's opening World Grand Prix scene, from an empty save, with movies on:**
  - A short START tap (0.2 s): the scene plays on to its end.
  - START held for 1.2 s: the SKIP circle appears and fills about halfway, then drains when START is let go, and the scene plays on.
  - START held for 2 s: the circle fills and the scene is skipped.

releases.name: v0.10.66 — CPU difficulty for Free Race
releases.body:
## Changes

- **New: CPU difficulty (#420).** The launcher has a new option, **General › Gameplay › CPU difficulty**, with four levels:
  - **Newbie** and **Easy:** the computer racers can no longer ride far above their top speed, so they fall behind. Newbie holds them back more than Easy.
  - **Normal (original):** the original game. This is the default.
  - **Hard:** the computer racers keep pace with you and can pass you. If you break away from them, the ones behind you speed up to catch up.
  - It only changes the computer racers. Your own racer is the same at every level.
  - It only applies to an offline **Free Race**. Story, the other modes and online races stay as the original.
  - It works at every Race step rate, from 60 to 144 Hz.

releases.name: Nixport v1.2.304-alpha
releases.body:
**Nixport v1.2.304-alpha** — a test build for people who want to try it early.

> Published by hand: built and signed with the same key as v1.1.299-alpha and
> v1.0.267-alpha (upgrades install over them without uninstalling).

## Changelog (since v1.1.299-alpha)

### Gamepads

- **Single-player pad model** (replaces v1.1's player slots): exactly one physical
  pad feeds the game at a time. The pad you touch takes over automatically
  (last-active wins); the session drawer offers "use this pad" to pin a choice for
  the session. The effective pad and the on-screen controls merge into one player.
- **Fix: intermittent directional input**. After opening a menu or losing focus,
  sticks / D-pad / triggers now reach the game immediately at their current position —
  no more "only X works in the load screen" or "the first press does nothing".
  The old "stay blocked until centered" gate is gone (keys only).
- Rumble now always lands on the effective pad (Xbox-protocol pads don't expose
  motors to Android — enable "phone vibration" as the fallback).
- On-screen stale-state fix: a closed overlay can no longer pin the virtual stick
  over the physical one.

## Changelog (since v1.0.267-alpha)

### Gamepads

- **Player slots**: Player 1 = on-screen controls + one selected physical pad, merged.
  The in-game drawer (Input tab) now lists every physical pad under "Physical gamepads" —
  set one as Player 1, assign pads to Players 2-4, or unassign them. An explicit choice is
  remembered across sessions.
- **First input wins**: with no explicit choice, the first pad that actually produces
  input becomes Player 1. Phantom devices (e.g. HyperOS's `uinput-xiaomi`) no longer eat
  Player 1 and silence your Bluetooth pad in-game — the main fix of this build.
- **Rumble return path**: a game's rumble request travels back over NXP2 v3 and drives the
  pad's own motors (falls back to the phone's motor when the pad has none).
